articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine 👻 Echoes Beyond: A Little AI, A Lot of Memories, and the Voices Time Almost Forgot This is my submissi…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine 👻 Echoes Beyond: A Little AI, A Lot of Memories, and the Voices Time Almost Forgot Some ghosts don't haunt houses. They live in old photographs, forgotten voice recordings, handwritten letters, and stories we never got around to telling. This is my submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. 🕯️ What I Built I built Echoes Beyond, an offline-first AI memory preservation project that turns forgotten memories into meaningful, interactive stories. Imagine finding an old letter from your grandfather, a recording of your grandmother telling a childhood story, or a photograph whose story nobody remembers anymore.
articles.author: Jay Jain

articles.title: Haunted Terminal
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine A haunted terminal. Haunted.ps1 is a single PowerShell file that possesses your real shell. After every…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built A haunted terminal. Haunted.ps1 is a single PowerShell file that possesses your real shell. After every command you run, a ghost whispers a short, eerie comment about what you just did. It's written by a local Gemma model and typed onto the screen one character at a time, like breath fogging a window. I took "Ghost in the Machine" literally: the machine is your terminal, and the ghost is a model living inside it. Failed commands get a blood drip and a mournful whisper. Successful ones get something quieter and creepier. The prompt becomes ☠ ~\path › , and each new session opens with a small ghost and a few drips of blood. In Windows Terminal, the window becomes frosted glass.
articles.author: TAIL

articles.title: Corvus - Hacktoberfest '26
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Corvus is a haunted-terminal AI workspace that runs Gemma entirely on your own computer. You open it, p…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Corvus is a haunted-terminal AI workspace that runs Gemma entirely on your own computer. You open it, pick a Gemma model, and talk to it. The reply streams in word by word from your own machine, inside an interface that looks like a forgotten laboratory terminal decorated for the Day of the Dead. I read "Ghost in the Machine" literally. The ghost is Gemma, an intelligence that lives inside your laptop instead of in a distant data center. The look blends two traditions. Halloween brings the mystery: obsidian black, scanlines, ravens and ember light. Día de los Muertos brings the warmth: marigolds, papel picado banners and the idea that remembering is a way of keeping someone alive.
articles.author: Ashish Anand

articles.title: Build a Streaming AI Chat UI in React with shadcn/ui (2026 Guide)
articles.excerpt: Getting tokens from a model to the browser is the easy part. Every modern SDK does it in a few lines. The hard part is everything the user actually experiences while those tokens arrive: the view that…
articles.body: Getting tokens from a model to the browser is the easy part. Every modern SDK does it in a few lines. The hard part is everything the user actually experiences while those tokens arrive: the view that yanks them back to the bottom while they are trying to read, the Send button that does nothing while a reply runs, the paragraph that reflows every 40 milliseconds, the screen reader that either announces nothing or announces every single token. This guide builds a streaming chat interface in React that gets those details right. We will use shadcn/ui as the foundation, the Vercel AI SDK for the transport, and four open-source components from Cuelark UI for the parts shadcn does not ship: Conversation , Message , StreamingText and PromptInput .
articles.author: Cuelark

articles.body: Exploring CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 through a TryHackMe lab. Introduction October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, and honestly, this month has been quite interesting from a cybersecurity perspective. There have been plenty of vulnerabilities, attacks and security incidents worth paying attention to. But while going through TryHackMe, something particularly caught my attention: PHP2Shell . At first, I was interested in the upload exploitation technique. I mean, how does something as ordinary as a file upload eventually lead to remote code execution? That question made me curious enough to investigate further. On October 21, 2026, two critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in PHP: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 .

articles.title: Socratic Duck
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine You know the rubber duck trick. You explain your bug out loud to a toy on your desk, and somewhere in t…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built You know the rubber duck trick. You explain your bug out loud to a toy on your desk, and somewhere in the middle of the sentence you hear yourself and the problem just falls out. The duck never says a word. That's the whole trick. AI tools quietly broke that. Now I paste the error, get a fix, and move on without learning why it broke. I did this for months before I noticed I was getting faster and not any better. So I built the opposite. Socratic Duck reads your code or a screenshot of your error and asks you questions. Only questions. There's a four step hint ladder, and it starts at "what did you expect to happen?" and slowly gets pointier,It never reaches the fix.

articles.title: 12 Years Later, Sofia Coppola's Unmade Epic Fantasy Still Lives Rent Free in My Head
articles.excerpt: Sofia Coppola, it’s not too late to make your dark take on The Little Mermaid
articles.body: The year was 2014. The live-action Disney remake craze had already begun thanks to the success of Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland , but it hadn’t reached its box office peak. Meanwhile, on the other side of Hollywood, Sofia Coppola was attached to a movie bursting at the seams with possibilities: a live-action The Little Mermaid, not based on the 1998 Disney animated classic, but on the original Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, where (spoiler alert) the brokenhearted mermaid dies by flinging herself into the ocean and dissolving into sea foam. I can picture Coppola’s compositions clearly in my mind: the mermaid (Elle Fanning) shot in pastel colors, thoughtfully looking out at the horizon. A song by The Strokes or Phoenix plays in the background.

articles.body: Anker is one of the top brands for charging tech, and likely one of the first places someone might look for a portable charger to go with a brand-new phone, or if their long-running handset needs a little help lasting a full day away from the outlet. So I was hoping that when I received the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro () in the mail, it would become one of the top picks from one of the top brands. Turns out that I’m half right. With a compact frame, built-in fan cooling, and the fastest Qi2 charging speeds on offer, the MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro seems like an ideal option. articles.body: Niagara Launcher is undoubtedly one of the best Android home screens you can run on a modern Android phone. It’s nippy, loaded with features, and rewards both minimalists and maximalists with its thoughtful feature set. Through its obvious and lesser-known features, I’ve used it to build a brilliant productivity setup that piloted my phone for years . There’s not too much criticism I could level against Niagara, but one thing does stand out. I regularly see posts online from users lamenting the pricing of its Pro version. I was lucky enough to board the Niagara boat early, and snagged it on the cheap during its beta phase.

articles.body: These days, Rockstar Games is one of the most famous developers in the world. That’s primarily thanks to their magnum opus, the Grand Theft Auto series, but also the Red Dead Redemption games, and to a lesser extent, L.A. Noire and the Max Payne series. In just a few short weeks, Grand Theft Auto 6 will finally be here, a game that has felt like a distant dream for so long, after delays and a slow trickle of new information. But 20 years ago, Rockstar released one of its most unique games that has hints of the classic GTA formula, and it's a crying shame that there is still no sign of a sequel.

articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent another batch of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from California just after midnight on Halloween (Oct. 31).
articles.body: SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launch on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093. The record for a SpaceX first stage is 37 , set this past August by the booster B1067.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.

articles.title: An aquanaut comes home: Returning to Earth from an undersea 'space station'
articles.excerpt: After five days of living underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew return to terra firma, affected by higher pressures and the team's disconnection from home.
articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

articles.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).
